title: Hide computer startup complexity behind a facade
description: Booting a computer requires sequencing three subsystems in order: CPU.initialize(), Memory.load(), then HardDrive.spin(). ComputerFacade should expose a single pressStart() method that performs all three steps in the correct order. Callers should never need to touch the subsystems directly.
hints: ComputerFacade holds references to CPU, Memory, and HardDrive
pressStart() calls each subsystem in the correct order: CPU first, then Memory, then HardDrive
The subsystem classes are provided — only ComputerFacade needs implementing
issues: Callers must know about three separate subsystems and the exact order to initialise them
Any change to the boot sequence requires updating every call site
overallGoal: Use the Facade pattern to give callers a single pressStart() entry point that encapsulates the full boot sequence, hiding all subsystem details.
goals: pressStart() calls CPU.initialize(), Memory.load(), and HardDrive.spin() in that order
Callers interact only with ComputerFacade, never with the subsystems directly
Each subsystem step is invoked exactly once per pressStart() call
